# Does this TSID work prove that whole-body torque control can run directly on any high-ratio humanoid without using any force sensor?

> **Current answer:** The method avoids joint-torque sensors by estimating torque from position-servo error and feeding it to TSID. It still uses wrist/ankle six-axis force sensors, an IMU, and encoders, while the paper's experiments cover only six joints of HRP-2's right leg in controlled free-motion and contact settings. It is therefore neither sensorless nor a plug-and-play cross-platform whole-body torque controller.

## Applicable robots

- HRP-2; transfer to another actuator requires new identification

## Controllers and methods

## Applicable environments

- Controlled HRP-2 single-leg free motion and rigid-contact experiments

## Assumptions

- The mapping from position error to torque for each high-ratio joint has been identified on the target hardware.
- Wrist/ankle force sensors, encoders, and the IMU remain available and calibrated.

## Result

- The method avoids joint-torque sensors by estimating torque from position-servo error and feeding it to TSID. It still uses wrist/ankle six-axis force sensors, an IMU, and encoders, while the paper's experiments cover only six joints of HRP-2's right leg in controlled free-motion and contact settings. It is therefore neither sensorless nor a plug-and-play cross-platform whole-body torque controller.

## Limitations

- The mapping from position error to torque for each high-ratio joint has been identified on the target hardware.
- Wrist/ankle force sensors, encoders, and the IMU remain available and calibrated.
